tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Physico-chemical properties of the designed Trp-rich peptides (TRPs).
footnotes: * Underlined and bold amino acids are D-enantiomers. The C terminus is amidated except for PuroA-OH peptide. ND: not determined. GRAVY: grand average of hydropathy.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Antimicrobial activities of peptides.
footnotes: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined as the lowest concentration of peptide that inhibited bacterial or yeast growth. * Data are mode of three independent experiments; ** Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus; N/T: not tested.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Salt tolerance, protease stability and DNA binding properties of peptides.
footnotes: * Up to 50 mM: no effects on antibacterial activity up to 50 mM NaCl but increase in the MICs for E. coli and S. aureus at 100 mM NaCl; intolerant = not resistant to salt effects even at 50 mM NaCl. Up to 150 mM: no effects on antibacterial activity up to 150 mM NaCl. ** Proteases tested: porcine trypsin and proteinase K.

tables.caption: Cytotoxicity of peptides to NIH-3T3 and HeLa cells.
footnotes: * IC50: concentration causing 50% cell growth inhibition. ** Therapeutic index = ratio of IC50 NIH-T3T (μg/mL) to IC50 HeLa (μg/mL) [34]. ND = not determined. “<” indicates the maximum TI calculated with 250 μg/mL. “>” indicates the minimum TI calculated with 250 μg mL−1, i.e., no IC50 values can be calculated within the tested concentration range of peptides (0–250 μg/mL). Results are the mean of triplicate assays.
